sph_interpretive_translation: For those whose fathers have passed away, the share of inheritance is determined directly from the father's lineage.
jurisprudential_principles: Inheritance rights are consciousness-bound, not material constructs
Capacity to inherit is derived from ancestral alignment
Restoration of familial dharma supersedes external claimants
executable_legal_axioms: IF deceased male lineage holder EXISTS THEN property devolves automatically to recognized male descendant(s)
IF no direct male descendant THEN revert to nearest patrilineal cognate within three generations
EXCLUDE all claims NOT validated by paternal acknowledgment OR ancestral registry
ENSURE continuity of family dharma THROUGH uninterrupted male succession
PREVENT fragmentation of estate BY prioritizing unity of inheritance
supreme_court_application: Supreme adjudication shall recognize only paternally authenticated succession, bypassing equitable distribution models. Courts must validate ancestral alignment prior to execution of inheritance directives.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Causality follows patrilineal pramāṇa; inheritance is not reward or penalty but continuation of dharma. Responsibility lies in maintaining ancestral flow, not assigning fault. Outcomes align with natural succession, not corrective justice.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Re-establish connection between heir and ancestral consciousness
Facilitate completion of unfinished duties of the departed through designated successor
Ensure ritual and material continuity without dispute generation
Integrate new heir into familial dharma cycle via ceremonial recognition
Neutralize competing claims through clarity of patrilineal record
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Inheritance flows from consciousness unbroken. Justice serves restoration alone. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate arbiter.
